levels.name: Partial
levels.description: AI takes over part of the job, but not all of it

L0.say: The AI note-taker trial came and went. Clinic runs the way it always did.
L0.think: Clinical judgement isn't going anywhere. My training still pays off.
L0.do: Keeps the same workload, skips the sales demos and trains junior doctors.
L0.feel: Settled. Tired from the rota, not from the future.

L1.say: The AI note-taker writes my notes now. I get ten more minutes with each patient.
L1.think: Documentation was never the job. Diagnosis and the conversation are.
L1.do: Joins the hospital's AI group and checks the note-taker's mistakes.
L1.feel: Quietly hopeful, but a little worried about who's to blame if it goes wrong.

L2.say: If diagnosis is automated by 2036, I need to be the one who signs it off.
L2.think: Doctors who supervise the systems keep their standing. The rest won't.
L2.do: Takes a course in medical technology and asks to help oversee the AI.
L2.feel: Uneasy, but there is time to position myself.

L3.say: Five years. My junior doctors are asking whether to finish training.
L3.think: My income depends on procedures and sign-off, and both are shrinking.
L3.do: Moves savings into lower-risk assets and negotiates a fixed-term contract.
L3.feel: Anxious about the team more than about myself.

L4.say: When the AI gets it wrong in 2028, who takes the blame? Not the company that sold it.
L4.think: The profession needs a seat at the table before decisions are made for us.
L4.do: Organises colleagues through the medical association and delays a house move.
L4.feel: Alarmed and angry at how fast this is landing.

L0.say: No AI rescue, then. Back to the eighty-hour weeks.
L0.think: The bottleneck is staffing, not software.
L0.do: Picks up extra shifts and studies for specialist exams.
L0.feel: Exhausted, but sure of the path.

L1.say: The AI triages faster than I do. My job is to check it.
L1.think: If the machine does the thinking, how do I learn to think?
L1.do: Asks seniors to keep teaching hands-on assessment.
L1.feel: Unsure whether the training still adds up.

L2.say: By the time I'm a consultant, the job could be gone.
L2.think: Ten years of training for a role that may not exist in 2036.
L2.do: Looks at a move into public health or clinical research.

L3.say: Why finish specialty training if it ends in 2031?
L3.think: Patients will still need care. They may not need me.
L3.do: Puts specialist training on hold and joins a union campaign for safe staffing.
L3.feel: Alarmed. My cohort talks about little else.

L4.say: I owe more than I'll ever earn as a doctor now.
L4.think: We were told to study medicine because it was safe.
L4.do: Applies for jobs abroad and in health tech, and pushes for loan relief.

L0.say: I've seen four of these revolutions. Paper won every time.
L0.think: Experience matters more than any algorithm.
L0.do: Carries on as usual and plans to retire in 2032.

L1.say: Fine, let it write the letters. I'll still see the patient.
L1.think: Useful for admin. Not to be trusted with judgement.
L1.do: Lets the juniors run the tools and signs off without using them.

L2.say: I'll be retired before it matters. The young ones should worry.
L2.think: My pension is secure. The profession's future is not.
L2.feel: Calm for myself, uneasy for the profession.

L3.say: Selling my share of the practice before 2031 is the only sensible move.
L3.think: The practice loses value every year the machines get better.
L3.do: Looks for a buyer for his share and mentors a successor.
L3.feel: Uneasy about selling at the wrong moment.

L4.say: My practice will be worth nothing in two years. Who buys it now?
L4.think: My retirement plan relied on the practice being worth something.
L4.do: Lobbies the medical regulator and covers shifts at other clinics to fill the gap.

L0.say: We're still short of doctors. Nothing has changed out here.
L0.think: Rural care needs people who stay.

L1.say: Remote triage cut my waiting list in half.
L1.think: If the tools reach the villages, I can do more good.
L1.do: Pilots the triage tool and trains the nurses on it.

L2.say: The health board will fund software before it funds another GP.
L2.think: Salaried doctors are the easiest line to cut.
L2.do: Takes on minor surgery to stay hard to replace.
L2.feel: Uneasy about the next budget round.

L3.say: Two clinics, one doctor and a chatbot. That's the plan for 2031.
L3.think: Patients out here will get the worst of the automated system.
L3.do: Writes to the local MP and joins the rural health network.
L3.feel: Alarmed for patients and for the job.

L4.say: My contract ends next year and nobody is renewing anything.
L4.think: A mortgage, and a salary that might not exist in 2028.
L4.do: Applies for any clinical role with a long contract.

L0.say: The pricing model never beat our judgement on complex risks.
L0.think: Unusual, complex risks still need a person to sign off.
L0.do: Writes business as usual and grows broker relationships.

L1.say: The model drafts the quote. I decide what we actually take on.
L1.think: Routine lines are gone. Complex risk is where I earn my keep.
L1.do: Moves fully into insuring complex and disaster risks.

L2.say: If pricing is automated by 2036, my value is the broker relationships.
L2.think: Relationships and judgement on unusual risks are all that protects my job.
L2.do: Takes a data science course and builds a book of complex accounts.

L3.say: Our team went from twelve to five this year.
L3.think: Bonuses follow volume, and the volume is going to the model.
L3.do: Talks to recruiters at larger insurers and at teams that check AI models.

L4.say: The board wants software to handle every policy, start to finish, by 2028.
L4.think: My know-how is turning into data to train the AI.
L4.do: Negotiates a deal to stay on and starts advising other firms on the side.

L0.say: I'm still learning the trade the old way.
L0.think: The seniors here will teach me for years.

L1.say: The model does the files I'd normally learn on. I review its work.
L1.think: I'm not sure I'm building real skill.
L1.do: Asks for complex files and learns Python at weekends.

L2.say: Junior roles here won't last another ten years.
L2.think: I need to move toward the model, not away from it.
L2.do: Applies to move into the team that sets prices from data.

L3.say: They cancelled the graduate scheme. I was in the last intake.
L3.think: There's no ladder above me to climb.
L3.do: Retrains in risk data and works hard on building contacts.

L4.say: I'll be replaced before I finish my exams.
L4.think: My degree was for a job that won't exist in 2028.
L4.do: Applies across sectors and moves back home to save.

L0.say: Twenty-two years in this job. It's not changing now.
L0.think: They need people who know the old policies.
L0.do: Keeps her head down and counts down to her pension.

L1.say: The system clears most of my files before I open them.
L1.think: The work I used to do is drying up.
L1.do: Volunteers for the unusual cases the system can't handle.

L2.say: I just need to hold on until I can retire.
L2.think: Ten years is about how long I need.
L2.do: Avoids attention and turns down a retraining offer.

L3.say: The offer is early retirement or redundancy. Neither covers the mortgage.
L3.think: Nobody will hire me at sixty for something new.
L3.do: Asks the union about severance terms.

L4.say: They told us on a group call. Two years and the department is gone.
L4.think: My pension won't stretch, and I don't know where to start.
L4.do: Cuts all spending and signs up for a free retraining scheme.

L0.say: Shame. The tools could have taken the drudge work.
L0.think: We'll keep spending expert time on admin.

L1.say: I run three models side by side and pick the best quote.
L1.think: This is the most interesting the job has ever been.
L1.do: Becomes the team's AI lead and trains colleagues.

L2.say: Ten years is plenty of time to move into model oversight.
L2.think: Someone has to govern these models, and I know the risks.
L2.do: Takes a qualification in checking AI models for risk.

L3.say: I'm safe. Half my friends in claims aren't.
L3.think: The gains should be shared, not just booked as savings.
L3.do: Pushes leaders for a fund that moves staff into new jobs.
L3.feel: Uneasy about the people left behind.

L4.say: Even the people building the models are on short contracts now.
L4.think: At this speed, oversight roles get cut too.
L4.do: Builds a consulting practice and saves a year's salary.

L0.say: They promised driverless trucks ten years ago. Still waiting.
L0.think: Roads, weather and docks are too messy for a computer.
L0.do: Keeps driving and adds a hazardous-goods licence.

L1.say: The truck handles the motorway. I handle the docks and the city.
L1.think: The long stretches get easier. The hard miles are still mine.

L2.say: By 2036 the long haul is automated. I'll take the local runs.
L2.think: Last-mile and specialist loads will last longest.
L2.do: Gets certified for oversize and hazardous loads.

L3.say: Freight rates are falling and the depot is cutting drivers.
L3.think: Self-driving fleets will undercut every independent driver.
L3.do: Joins the drivers' association and sells his second truck.

L4.say: I've still got four years left on the truck loan.
L4.think: Nobody will pay me to drive what a robot drives for free.
L4.do: Looks into warehouse supervisor and rail jobs.

L0.say: Got my licence last year. There's plenty of work.
L0.do: Builds hours toward a better-paying route.

L1.say: The scanner tells me every move. I'm the robot's hands.
L1.think: The skilled part of the job is going first.
L1.do: Asks for forklift and dispatch training.

L2.say: I'm twenty-four. This job ends before I'm thirty-five.
L2.think: I need a trade the machines can't reach.

L3.say: Agency shifts dropped by half this year.
L3.think: If I'm not out by 2031, I'm stuck.
L3.do: Moves to night shifts to pay for training.

L4.say: My hours were cut to two days a week.
L4.think: There's no time left to retrain properly.
L4.do: Takes any gig work going and moves in with family.

L0.say: Thirty years on the road. The road hasn't changed.

L1.say: Too many screens in the cab now. I miss just driving.
L1.think: The young ones will adapt. I'm not sure I want to.

L2.say: I'll be retired by then. Probably.
L2.think: I just need the pension to hold.

L3.say: The company wants volunteers for early exit. I might take it.
L3.think: A buyout now beats being pushed out later.
L3.do: Has the union check the severance terms.

L4.say: I can't retire in two years, and nobody hires a sixty-year-old driver.
L4.think: There's no bridge to my pension.
L4.do: Joins a protest convoy and writes to his MP.

L0.say: No change. Specialist loads always needed a human.
L0.think: Heavy-haul and hazardous skills are rare.

L1.say: I supervise three assisted trucks from my cab now.
L1.think: Supervising automation pays better than driving.

L2.say: Somebody has to run the automated fleet. That's my next ten years.
L2.think: Fleet oversight is the safest seat.
L2.do: Moves into the remote control room.

L3.say: The remote control room has one person for twenty trucks.
L3.think: Even the oversight jobs are thinning.
L3.do: Studies for a logistics management diploma.

L4.say: My specialty buys me maybe a year longer than the rest.
L4.think: Hazardous loads are the last to go, but they go.
L4.do: Saves hard and plans a move into safety inspection.

L0.say: The AI tutors faded out after one term.
L0.think: Teaching is relationships. That hasn't changed.
L0.do: Keeps refining lessons the usual way.

L1.say: AI marks the quizzes. I spend the time on the students who are struggling.
L1.do: Builds AI feedback into her lessons.

L2.say: If AI tutors take over by 2036, what is school for?
L2.think: Teachers become coaches and carers, or nothing.
L2.do: Trains to design courses and to lead student wellbeing.

L3.say: My class sizes doubled while the tutor licences got renewed.
L3.think: The budget follows the software, not the children.
L3.do: Joins union negotiations on staffing ratios.

L4.say: Who looks after the children when screens do the teaching?
L4.think: Children will lose the adults in their lives.
L4.do: Campaigns with parents and looks at counselling training.

L0.think: I'll get to a full teaching post in time.

L1.say: The AI does the reading support I was hired for.
L1.think: My role is the first to shrink.
L1.do: Moves toward supporting children with special needs.

L2.say: Why qualify for a job that changes completely by 2036?
L2.think: I'll need more than classroom skills.

L3.say: Support staff contracts weren't renewed this summer.
L3.think: My income is the first thing the school cuts.
L3.do: Takes tutoring gigs and childcare shifts.

L4.say: I'm out of work by next year, and so is everyone I trained with.
L4.think: Nobody planned for people like us.
L4.do: Applies for care work and retail jobs.

L0.say: Good. Children need books and a teacher at the front.
L0.think: Discipline and knowledge still matter most.

L1.say: The software marks the homework. I still read every essay.
L1.think: Pupils are learning to ask machines, not to think.
L1.do: Bans AI tools in his department's exams.

L2.say: I'll be gone before the robots take my classroom.
L2.think: My pension will be fine. The next generation won't.
L2.do: Mentors new staff on classroom management.

L3.say: They want me to supervise four AI classrooms at once.
L3.think: This isn't teaching. It's crowd control.

L4.say: Two years to dismantle a profession that took a century to build.
L4.do: Writes to the school board and the parents' association.

L0.say: Our parents pay for teachers, and that's what they get.

L1.say: AI does the marking and the teaching stays human. Parents love it.
L1.think: AI frees teachers for the valuable part.

L2.say: Human teaching will become a premium product.
L2.think: The best schools will sell what AI can't.

L3.say: Even fee-paying parents ask why they're paying for teachers.
L3.think: Premium only lasts while outcomes stay ahead.
L3.do: Rebuilds the curriculum around projects and debate.

L4.say: Enrolments fell twenty percent after the tutor app launched.
L4.think: We have two years to prove what a teacher is for.
L4.do: Cuts costs and rebuilds the school around one-to-one mentoring.

say: We trialled the AI tools. They didn't stick.
It handles the {task}. The {core} is still mine.
By 2036 even the {core} is automated. I have ten years to plan.
Two years until the {core} goes too. Tell me what to do now.

early: My skills will carry a whole career.
Better to learn the tools now, while it's cheap to.
I'll need a second skill before 2036.
Starting over at thirty beats starting over at forty.
There's no career left to start.
mid: My skills stay valuable for the foreseeable future.
Parts of my job will shrink. The core stays.
I need a second skill before the decade is out.
My mortgage will outlast my job.
Everything I built my career on is going.
late: I'll finish my career doing what I know.
I can ride this out until retirement.
Retirement might arrive just in time.
My pension plan assumed ten more years.

high: Keeps the current routine and skips optional AI training.
Pays for a specialist course and hands routine work to AI.
Spreads out savings and looks at related jobs.
Hires a career coach and negotiates a deal to stay on.
Moves savings into cash and starts freelance advising.
medium: Keeps the current routine and skips optional AI training.
Takes a short course and offloads routine tasks.
Saves more and looks at related jobs.
Retrains at night and joins an industry group.
Cuts spending and applies outside the sector.
low: Keeps the current routine and skips optional AI training.
Learns the tools on the job, unpaid.
Picks up extra hours to build a savings buffer.
Takes a second job and looks for funded retraining.
Signs up for job support and takes any work going.

feel.calm: Work feels the same as last year.
feel.uneasy: Curious, with a low hum of worry.
feel.anxious: Pressure building, but still in control.
feel.alarmed: Losing sleep over what comes next.
feel.panicked: Overwhelmed, angry and out of time.

templates.feelCalmLater: Calm, with a plan in place.
